sovereign_country.strategic_role: 苏伊士运河经济特区、辐射中东及北非的低成本轻工制造

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Building Information Modeling (BIM) and Structural Drafting

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law system with Islamic Sharia as the principal source of legislation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: US-Egypt Bilateral Investment Treaty (entered into force 1992)
China-Egypt Agreement on Investment Promotion and Reciprocal Protection (1994/1997)
UK-Egypt Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (1975)
Egypt-UAE Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments
Egypt-EU Euro-Mediterranean Association Agreement (2004), including investment and trade protection

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 95 of 2003; Law No. 72 of 2023 on Companies (as amended) and GAFI directives requiring beneficial owner identification for LLC incorporation; Central Bank of Egypt AML/CFT Rules and the Financial Regulatory Authority UBO instructions for non-banking financial sectors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the passport or national ID of each member/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary public of the member's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian Embassy/Consulate (Egypt is not an Apostille contracting state)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing / corporate extract of any corporate shareholder or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization by the Egyptian diplomatic post in the issuing jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Arabic memorandum of association and articles of association of the LLC
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Egyptian Notary Public Department (Ministry of Justice)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Egypt and registration with GAFI/Commercial Registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form, organizational chart and source-of-funds statement executed by shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: LLC shareholders or their legal representatives
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization plus Consular Legalization if executed outside Egypt

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every UBO, director, manager and authorized signatory against the Egyptian FIU and Central Bank of Egypt sanctions/terrorism-financing lists, the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Consolidated List, EU sanctions list and domestic watchlists. PEPs, both domestic and foreign, must be identified at onboarding, risk-rated, and subjected to enhanced due diligence including verification of source of wealth and funds. Negative-news and adverse-media screening are required, with findings escalated to the Money Laundering Reporting Officer before incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI e-Investment and Companies Establishment Portal, integrated with the Egyptian Commercial Registry (Ministry of Justice/Investment) for electronic name reservation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be reserved in Arabic as the governing corporate designation. A Latin-script transliteration/translation may be registered for foreign use, but the Arabic name must be neither descriptive-only nor conflict with an existing registered name. The name must not violate public order, mimic Egyptian governmental bodies, or use non-Arabic scripts as the primary name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, an electronic rejection notice is issued citing the conflicting name or prohibited token. The applicant must file an administrative appeal with GAFI's Legal Affairs Department within fifteen working days, attaching a certified valid name-search report, a memorandum distinguishing the requested mark, and a fallback name. If GAFI upholds the rejection, an appeal may be brought before the Administrative Court in Cairo under the Administrative Judiciary Law. The applicant should immediately reserve an alternative name in parallel to avoid blocking incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A standalone virtual/mail-drop office is not permissible for a GAFI-registered LLC. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt suitable for service of process and statutory records. A serviced office with a dedicated unit, physical signage, and a lease is acceptable for an offshore BIM/CAD outsourcing business; fully remote 'virtual-only' seats do not satisfy commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% to 20% annual likelihood for a low-risk professional-services LLC; unannounced inspection is most likely after tax registration or bank account opening, and may verify physical premises, signboard, personnel, and transactional substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended by Law No. 4 of 2022, including the provisions applicable to Limited Liability Companies; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registration Law provisions relating to registration of companies with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration and Commercial Registry One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association (Aqd Al-Shirkah) submitted electronically through GAFI, culminating in the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qaid Al-Tijari).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Under the amended Companies Law, an LLC is not subject to a prescribed statutory minimum capital. The founding members must declare an initial capital in the memorandum, which must be fully paid into a temporary blocked escrow bank account in the company's name and held until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued, after which the funds are released to the company treasury.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved: (1) Share Subscription: The founding members subscribe to the entire LLC capital of EGP 50,000, being 100 ordinary shares at EGP 500 each; the bank certificate of full payment into the escrow account is adopted as conclusive evidence of capital contribution. (2) Registered Office: The registered office is fixed at 12 Mohamed Basha Street, Cairo, Egypt; the managers shall effect all filings with GAFI and the Commercial Registry. (3) Officer Appointments: The founding members are appointed managers, jointly and severally authorised to open bank accounts, sign regulatory submissions, engage counsel and accountants, and obtain tax cards, commercial registrations, and social-insurance clearances, pending the first audited annual accounts. Adopted this [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop – Egyptian General Authority for Investment and Free Zones online incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the GAFI investor portal; select 'Limited Liability Company'; request a name clearance certificate for the proposed Arabic/English company name, with three alternatives. Upload the required identification, pay the statutory clearance fee, and download the approved name certificate. This certificate remains valid for 60 days and must be attached to the memorandum.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all founding members and ultimate beneficial owners
Three proposed company names in Arabic and/or English
Signed authorization letter appointing the authorized incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registered company or trademark, submit an appeal to GAFI Legal Affairs and simultaneously propose three new alternative names; GAFI issues a revised decision within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Capital Escrow and Contribution Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional capital escrow account in the future LLC name; deposit the full stated capital; obtain a bank certificate confirming that the account is blocked from withdrawal until presentation of the Certificate of Incorporation. The bank will conduct customer due diligence and anti-money-laundering screening on all signatories.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Name clearance certificate
Passport copies and proof of address for each member
Source-of-funds and AML declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide certified source-of-funds documentation and a notarized undertaking; re-submit within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Notary Public Office (Tawteeq)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary, or through a duly notarized power of attorney, to execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association; verify the Arabic text and pay the applicable stamp duty. The notary endorses the document as the foundational incorporation instrument.
required_dossiers: Bank capital escrow certificate
Name clearance certificate
Draft memorandum and articles in Arabic
Lease or title deed for the registered office
Passport copies and specimen signatures of signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags defective or inconsistent clauses, execute an amendment deed before the same notary and resubmit the corrected version to GAFI within seven working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing with GAFI and Commercial Registry Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / Commercial Registry One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Memorandum and Articles, bank escrow certificate, and registered-office declaration through the GAFI One-Stop Shop. GAFI verifies legal compliance, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, and registers the LLC in the Commercial Register with a unique commercial registration number. The incorporation takes effect on the date of that registration.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital escrow certificate
Name clearance certificate
Registered office lease or ownership document
First board resolution appointing managers
Passport copies of managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI raises a compliance remark, submit a supplementary declaration and, where necessary, amend the articles; a corrected filing is adjudicated within 10 working days without losing the original priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) and National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) – mixed registration branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, file for a tax card, employer tax number, and VAT certificate with the competent ETA office; concurrently register the company as an employer and register payroll with the NOSI. Establish the statutory chart of accounts and appoint an external auditor where required by law.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial registration certificate
Lease contract and registered-office proof
Board resolution appointing tax representative and auditor
Passport copies and address proof of the responsible officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ETA delays issuance of a tax card pending address verification, produce the utility bill with the company postal address and request reinspection; NOSI registration must be completed within one month of incorporation to avoid penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Occupational Premises Clearance and Civil Defense Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Administration of Civil Defense (Fire Safety Department) and the competent district municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For the administrative office, submit floor plans, the landlord's fire-safety compliance statement, and an evacuation plan to the Civil Defense authority. Obtain a fire and occupancy inspection and ensure structural load certification covers the intended CAD workstation density. This clearance is a workplace safety certification, not an industrial manufacturing license.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Lease or ownership deed
Architectural floor plans and site plan
Fire alarm and extinguisher maintenance contract
Structural load certificate for the floor
Occupational health and safety policy statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an inspection identifies noncritical defects, submit a corrective action plan, remedy the defects, and request a re-inspection; Civil Defense issues the certificate upon demonstrated compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA) – not applicable to the current non-industrial CAD/BIM service scope; would only apply if a future physical manufacturing or workshop facility is established.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required – ISIC 7110 office-based Building Information Modeling and structural drafting does not require an industrial operating permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category D administrative and professional service office; no full EIA report or registration is required for pure CAD/BIM drafting activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, volatile organic compound, or industrial waste streams are generated. Sanitary discharges must comply with Ministerial Decree No. 44/2000 wastewater discharge limits into municipal sewerage; domestic solid waste must be collected only by licensed municipal waste contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense; structural load clearance for floor loading; workplace occupational safety inspection by the competent labor authority; emergency lighting, evacuation signage, and fire extinguisher servicing under the Egyptian Fire Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — the unified national revenue agency of Egypt; primary portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoice, e-receipt and e-filing platform: https://www.invoice.eta.gov.eg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the foreign-owned LLC with GAFI (General Authority for Investment) and obtain the Commercial Registry certificate. 2) Submit the tax registration application (Tax Card/TIN) to the ETA territorial tax office under the Unified Tax Procedures Law 206/2020, including the certified Arabic incorporation deed, commercial registry extract, leasing/business-address evidence, passport copies of members, board resolution appointing an Egyptian tax representative, and opening bank confirmation. 3) File a separate VAT registration application on the ETA portal once actual or expected annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000, or elect voluntary VAT registration when exporting zero-rated services. 4) Activate the ETA e-invoicing account and obtain the PKI digital-signature certificate for FATORA clearance. Trackable turnaround typically 10–20 business days after complete submission.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Egyptian LLC is a resident juridical person taxed independently under Income Tax Law 91/2005 (standard CIT 22.5%); no pass-through eligibility for LLC members.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists in Egypt. Statutory elections available: (a) voluntary VAT registration for exporters below the EGP 500,000 compulsory threshold (Law 67/2016, Art. 78); (b) group tax consolidation for wholly-owned Egyptian subsidiaries upon ETA approval (Law 91/2005, Art. 60); (c) treaty relief/advance pricing applications for cross-border engineering service income; (d) free-zone or Special Economic Zone status (e.g., SCZone) election if the LLC relocates operations into an approved zone; (e) anti-hybrid-related deduction restrictions under the GAAR clauses of Law 91/2005 (Art. 59) disallow payments to tax-exempt or hybrid-entity related persons.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, and its Executive Regulations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 aggregate annual taxable supplies for compulsory VAT registration (Law 67/2016, Art. 78); no threshold for non-resident digital or e-commerce service suppliers; exporters may voluntarily register below the threshold to claim refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory ETA-governed e-invoicing and e-receipt regime per Ministerial Decrees 188/2021, 123/2022 and 127/2022, phased for all VAT-registered enterprises; invoices/receipts must be transmitted in real time to the FATORA platform (https://www.invoice.eta.gov.eg) in ETA-compliant XML, digitally signed with ETA-issued PKI certificates, validated synchronously via API, and stamped with a unique QR code; paper or non-cleared invoices are legally null and attract administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to export of goods and to services supplied to a non-resident recipient where the service is wholly performed or consumed outside Egypt, the consideration is received in convertible foreign currency remitted into an Egyptian bank account, and the offshore utilization is evidenced; for EG_LLC's offshore BIM/CAD deliverables, the contract must specify exclusive use of outputs outside Egypt, the recipient must be non-resident, and delivery/utilization must occur outside Egyptian territory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Certified export contract naming the non-resident client and stating offshore delivery of CAD/BIM services
Egyptian Customs export declaration (SAD) for any physical deliverables or media shipped abroad
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical movement out of Egypt when applicable
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or authenticated SWIFT MT103 proving the foreign-currency consideration entered an Egyptian bank account

ETA zero-rating substantiation file: serialized commercial invoice matching the cleared e-invoice XML, offshore service acceptance certificate, non-resident tax-residency certificate of the client, and utilization logs (IP access, deliverable handover) confirming consumption abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA desk and field audits may re-characterize improperly documented exports as taxable local supplies, resulting in retroactive 14% VAT assessment plus delay tax at 2% per month or fraction thereof up to the statutory cap (100%), fines ranging from EGP 5,000 to EGP 100,000, and imprisonment up to 5 years under Law 67/2016 Arts. 73 and 76 for fraudulent zero-rating claims; invalid export documentation also nullifies the Egyptian recipient's input-credit entitlement and exposes the exporter to refund clawback plus interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates under a partial liberalization regime. Current account transactions are broadly convertible, while capital account remittances such as dividends, loan repayments, and capital repatriation require prior CBE registration, documentary substantiation, and passage through a licensed Egyptian bank under the post-2016 flexible exchange-rate framework. Profit remittances are freely permitted once audited financial statements and a tax clearance certificate are submitted. The underlying foreign-direct investment must be registered with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), and the incoming capital must be certified by the receiving bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be credited to an Egyptian bank account within 90 days from the date of shipment and are subject to a mandatory surrender ratio of 100% to the local bank unless the CBE grants a specific exemption, such as financing inputs or repayment of existing foreign currency obligations. The exporting company must submit the customs-related export declaration and the applicable CBE foreign-exchange form to evidence the underlying transaction.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. Offshore digital EMIs such as Wise or Payoneer are not licensed by the CBE and cannot maintain Egyptian pound accounts, receive EGP-cleared payments, or provide local virtual IBANs. Their use is restricted to inbound and outbound remittances in convertible currencies where the underlying funds originate from or settle to a licensed Egyptian bank. For treasury operations, a direct CBE-licensed bank account is legally required for all local-currency and EGP-denominated settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of the authorised signatories is generally mandatory at account opening. CBE-regulated banks require at least one director or a senior attorney-in-fact with a valid notarised power of attorney to attend in person for biometric verification. Remote KYC via video verification is permitted only for existing clients and cannot substitute the first-time customer due-diligence interview of non-resident shareholders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Injection of capital from a jurisdiction of concern through a third-party remitter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised board resolution, certified passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners, source-of-wealth statement, audited financial statements, source-account bank statement, underlying service contract, and GAFI registration certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated business activity (CAD/BIM drafting) and large cross-border payment flows to or from counterparties in high-risk sectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreement with clients, detailed invoices and time-sheet records, client corporate registry extract, professional liability insurance policy, and CBE foreign-exchange declarations for each wire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic activity in Egypt relative to offshore revenues.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts, payroll and social-insurance filings, office lease agreement, utility invoices, local bank account activity, and audited financial statements evidencing substantial local presence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All equity capital must be remitted from the shareholder's bank account to the entity's CBE-licensed bank in Egypt via SWIFT MT103. The transfer reference must state the company identifier and the purpose code for FDI equity. The receiving bank will complete the CBE foreign-exchange declaration, verify against GAFI registration, credit the capital escrow account, and issue a foreign-exchange certificate evidencing the conversion to EGP for subsequent profit-repatriation calculations. Source-funds documentation covering the shareholder's reserves must be retained for AML checks.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported inputs and overseas subcontractors are executed through SWIFT MT103 for direct payments or MT700 for commercial documentary credits, routed via the Egyptian bank. Each payment requires underlying invoices, purchase orders, customs declarations where goods cross borders, and the applicable CBE foreign-exchange form. Transactions relating to CAD/BIM services are classified as current account and are settled without prior approval once documentary proof of the service has been filed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts on USD/EGP and EUR/EGP with a licensed Egyptian bank, subject to an underlying trade or transactional exposure.
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP) for long-term project-related receivables, subject to CBE approval and documentation of the underlying obligation.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed by the non-resident parent or a financing affiliate, not by the Egyptian resident entity, to hedge EGP exposure without creating an onshore obligation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Reconciliation with Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) - National Tax E-Filing Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within four months after the end of the tax year; calendar-year LLC must file by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of EGP 10,000-EGP 40,000; monthly interest at 2% of the overdue corporate tax; enforced collection and tax inspection; prolonged non-compliance supports Commercial Registry strike-off of the company record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Value Added Tax Return and Settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Last day of the month immediately following each VAT tax period; monthly filing regime applies to the LLC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of 2% per month on unpaid VAT; delay fines of EGP 10,000-EGP 40,000 for omitted or late returns; administrative attachment for persistent non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (Ministry of Justice) via GAFI One-Stop Services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the statutory renewal calendar each year, customarily from 1 January through 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal penalties accrue daily; the Commercial Registry may suspend activities and, after sustained non-renewal, strike off the legal-entity record.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Employee Salary Tax Withholding Payment and Annual Payroll Tax Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly withholding payment by the 15th day of the following month; annual reconciliation submitted with the corporate income tax return by the return due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 10,000-EGP 40,000 under Law No. 91 of 2005 plus 2% monthly interest; liability of LLC managers or officers for unremitted employee tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Social Insurance Contributions Declaration and Annual Insured-Wages List
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly declaration and payment within 15 days after each month-end; annual declaration at the start of the contribution year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment surcharge of 2% per month; assessed contributions on omission; collection enforcement against company assets and manager liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (EFIU) and Commercial Registry, as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the Commercial Registry renewal; immediate notification within the statutory period after any share transfer or beneficial-owner change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines and criminal sanctions under AML Law No. 80 of 2002 for incomplete or outdated UBO records; refusal of Commercial Registry renewal until records are corrected.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Assembly Resolution Approving Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: LLC shareholders' general assembly; minutes recorded in the statutory corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Managers must prepare the financial statements and convene the assembly within the statutory period after fiscal year-end, customarily by 31 March for a calendar-year LLC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Manager liability and fines under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; unapproved audited statements invalidate the corporate tax filing; continued default may be treated as non-compliance by the Commercial Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent audit is compulsory for every active Egyptian LLC regardless of turnover or asset size under Companies Law No. 159 of 1981; the shareholders may waive the external auditor only for a fully dormant fiscal year by unanimous shareholders' resolution. An LLC engaged in engineering CAD and BIM services is presumed active and must file Form No. 19 with audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) issued by the Ministry of Finance; EAS are IFRS-converged and binding for LLC statutory financial statements; listed and regulated entities must reconcile to full IFRS where required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday for ordinary engineering service LLCs. Under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, qualifying new projects outside the Valley and Delta may access preferential capital asset deductions and temporary rate abatements; a Free-Zone LLC may obtain 0% CIT on 100% export-oriented BIM/CAD services if approved by the General Authority for Investment (GAFI). The default effective rate remains 22.5% absent such incentives.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 21) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at www.incometax.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; quarterly advance CIT payments are required based on the preceding fiscal year's tax liability where the prior-year tax exceeds the statutory threshold.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the close of the fiscal year. For a 31 December year-end, the filing deadline is 30 April; for fiscals ended 30 June, 31 October.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross engineering/CAD/BIM service revenue and other business receipts arising from Egypt and foreign clients attributable to the Egyptian LLC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders — not the LLC itself — should not file this form in their own names unless they carry on a permanent establishment (PE) in Egypt. Where the LLC is owned by a foreign investor, all Egyptian-source revenue of the LLC is reported here; if the LLC has no PE and is merely collecting contracted fees for an offshore principal, such fees should instead be subject to withholding and not entered as LLC revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs of service delivery: payroll of architects/engineers, software and platform expenses, subcontracted drafting services, depreciation of computers and technical equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only deductible if incurred for generating taxable revenue and evidenced by bank transfers, contracts, and e-invoices. Intra-group service charges paid to foreign affiliates must satisfy transfer pricing documentation and Egyptian economic substance principles before deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: General administrative expenses: rent, commercial registration renewals, professional fees, marketing, utilities, and insurance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owner's general and administrative costs cannot be recharged to the Egyptian LLC unless supported by an intercompany agreement and an arm's-length markup. Without Form No. 41 declarations and TP documentation, the ETA may disallow the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before adjustment: Box 1 minus Box 2 and Box 3, adjusted for non-deductible provisions, donations, and intercompany payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC is managed by non-resident directors and all strategic decisions are made outside Egypt, the ETA may deem the company to have a local PE and include global engineering revenues in this box unless the company can demonstrate Egyptian board meetings and substantive management in Egypt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory adjustments and add-backs: fines, bribery amounts, unrecognized provisions, excessive director salaries, non-deductible entertainment expenses, and withholding tax borne by the company on behalf of non-residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any Egyptian withholding tax assumed by the LLC as a contractual cost that should otherwise be deducted from a non-resident recipient must be added back; a non-resident recipient cannot obtain treaty relief indirectly through the Egyptian cost payer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable income: Box 4 plus Box 5, after applying available tax-loss carryforwards (maximum 5 years).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses incurred while the LLC is wholly foreign-owned are carried forward only if the LLC maintains a valid Egyptian tax card and continuous activity; failure to file annual returns suspends the carryforward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT at 22.5% on adjusted taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Flat rate applies to all Egyptian-source income of the LLC, regardless of non-resident ownership percentage. Treaty-protected income is captured only via separate withholding treatment and cannot be netted here absent a PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax prepayments: quarterly advance CIT payments, final withholding tax credits, and foreign tax credits for foreign-source revenue where a DTA permits credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to credit the LLC-level tax against their home-country tax except under the applicable DTA's foreign tax credit provisions. The LLC may claim credit for Egyptian taxes borne by a foreign PE only with Form TRC and separate country-by-country statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net CIT payable or refund claimed: Box 7 minus Box 8, after withholding tax and advance payment offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund claim is subject to ETA pre-audit and may be offset against tax debts of the LLC or, in limited cases, against withholding obligations on profit distribution to the non-resident shareholder.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a periodic fine not exceeding EGP 5,000 plus an incremental penalty for each month of default. Late payment of assessed CIT accrues a monthly surcharge of 0.5% of the unpaid amount. Aggravated assessments after a tax investigation can impose up to 20% additional tax on the understated tax, plus fines and imprisonment where evasion is proven.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on gross dividends distributed by an Egyptian LLC to resident and non-resident shareholders unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Agreement (DTA).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply DTA relief on profit repatriation, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain an authenticated Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) for the relevant calendar year from its home tax authority; (ii) complete ETA's simplified withholding relief form and deposit it with the withholding agent bank and the ETA before the remittance date; (iii) provide a declaration of beneficial ownership, showing no pass-through arrangement; and (iv) upon ETA endorsement, apply the reduced DTA rate rather than pay and reclaim. In practice, the Egyptian Egyptian Tax Authority conducts a substance review and may require board resolutions, ownership register extracts, and audited financial statements of the recipient.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 20% WHT on royalties and technical service fees and 10% on interest paid to non-residents. Under most Egyptian DTAs, interest is reduced to 10-15%, and royalties to 10-15%, subject to TRC and beneficial ownership certification. CAD/BIM software licensing fees are treated as royalties unless the substance is a purchase of standard software; platform subscription fees could be recharacterized as technical service fees and subject to 20% WHT absent treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 8,000,000 in aggregate related-party transactions in a fiscal year triggers mandatory Egyptian Transfer Pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) under the ETA Transfer Pricing Guidelines.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code. However, the ETA applies the OECD BEPS Action 6 beneficial-ownership and substance requirements to deny DTA and withholding relief. A CAD/BIM outsourcing LLC must demonstrate live Egyptian management decisions, a physical office, local technical staff and payroll, and real operational bank accounts in Egypt. Failing this, the structure may be disregarded, treaty benefits denied, and all revenue treated as Egyptian-source without cost deductions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Omission of Egyptian-Source Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Contracting with foreign clients directly from offshore accounts, failing to record engineering service receipts on the Egyptian books, or creating fake subcontractor invoices from shell companies to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax up to 25% of the hidden tax payable, fines under Law 91/2005 of up to EGP 50,000, and imprisonment for a term starting at two years. The ETA may also compulsorily reassess gross revenue at 22.5% CIT and disallow all contested deductions pending criminal proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who authorized concealment are jointly liable for the underpaid tax, interest, and fines; the tax authority can issue travel bans on the directors and the general manager pursuant to the Tax Collection Law and seek sequestration of personal assets, followed by imprisonment of controlling shareholders for criminal evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an Egyptian LLC as a nominal booking center with zero employees, no real office, no board meetings in Egypt, and transfer of all engineering decision-making to the non-resident parent while claiming Egyptian tax residency and treaty benefits on dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA may disregard the intercompany contracts and treat the LLC as fiscally nonexistent, reattributing 100% of the net profit to the foreign shareholder as Egyptian-source distributions subject to 10% dividend WHT and additional tax of up to 20% of the underassessed amount. The company's trade license may be suspended by GAFI, and all tax exemptions and incentives are revoked retroactively.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: On veil-piercing under Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 2020, directors and shadow managers are personally liable for the company's tax debt if they stripped assets or maintained fictitious capital. Courts may impose a travel ban, civil restitution of unpaid tax, and imprisonment for the de facto manager for issuing false invoices and obstructing tax inspection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing engineering service invoices through personal accounts of a non-resident nominee, revolving cash withdrawals by nominal local partner, accepting anonymous capital contributions, or failing to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner of the LLC to the Egyptian Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) and the ETA during tax audits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002: fines up to EGP 200,000 and imprisonment for up to three years, with confiscation of the laundered amounts and underlying assets. Licensed service providers involved in the transaction may be penalized with revocation or suspension, and the FIU may freeze corporate bank accounts immediately.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to ensure customer due diligence and beneficial ownership disclosure can be held personally liable for corporate AML fines and civil restitution. In aggravated cases involving cross-border AEDT-style engineering contracts, the public prosecutor can impose travel bans and pretrial detention on the directors while funds in Egyptian banks are sequestered.
